name: Right-wing dictatorship
summary: Right-wing dictatorship is a descriptive label for authoritarian or totalitarian regimes pursuing right-wing policies, usually tied to anti-communism, traditionalism, law and order and nationalism. No founding text or defining scholarship states positions on the test's statements; the sources opened discuss dictatorship in general or particular regimes.
scope: A regime-type label, not a doctrine with canonical texts. Britannica's entries define dictatorship, authoritarianism and military rule generally and do not use the term 'right-wing dictatorship'. Individual regimes (Franco, Pinochet, Nazi Germany) are other subjects, so their records are not used here.
